article.title: Getting started
article.p: This section of the documentation describes how to get hold of SaxonC and the PHP and Python extensions, how to install on the different platforms, and how to get started using it.
Please use the help forums ("Forums") and bug trackers ("Issues") in the SaxonC project at the Saxonica community site if you need help or advice, or want to provide any other feedback.

section.title: Installing SaxonC
section.p: SaxonC can be installed on Linux, Mac OS and Windows. As a prerequisite SaxonC requires as a minimum C++14. In this section we provide a step by step installation guide for the three platforms.
For information on installing the PHP and Python extensions see the PHP extension and Python extension sections.

section.title: Windows
section.aside: In the following, [EDITION] means one of: HE, PE, EE; and [VERSION] is the maintenance release version number (for instance 12.1).

li.p: Download the SaxonC software from www.saxonica.com. There are different downloads available for the Saxon-HE, Saxon-PE and Saxon-EE products, for different operating systems.
To install the SaxonC-[EDITION] release on Windows, run the installer executable libsaxon-[EDITION]-win-setup-v[VERSION].exe, and follow the installer steps.

During the installation process, you will be asked to select the destination folder, which is the directory in which the core SaxonC files will be installed. The default and recommended location is C:\Program Files\Saxonica\Saxon[EDITION][VERSION]. This is the location that the PHP extension looks for the SaxonC DLL library, so we advise using this default location.
If you choose to install to a different location, then the SAXONC_HOME variable must be set accordingly (see the next step).
If the SaxonC files were installed to a location other than the default C:\Program Files\Saxonica\Saxon[EDITION][VERSION], then the SAXONC_HOME variable must be set to the correct location.

section.title: Licensing
section.p: SaxonC-PE and SaxonC-EE are commercial products, and require a license key. By downloading the software, you agree to the terms and conditions published at https://www.saxonica.com/license/eval-license.pdf (for use with a free evaluation license) or https://www.saxonica.com/license/paid-license.pdf (in the case of paid-up licenses, purchased from our online store).
section.h3: Location of the Saxon license file
section.p: SaxonC looks in the path relative to where the main library has been installed. For example, in /usr/lib if this is where libsaxon[EDITION]c.so has been installed. Alternatively, Saxon also looks for the license according to the environment variable SAXONC_HOME, if this has been set.

Alternatively the licenseFileLocation configuration property can be used to provide the license location (see Configuration for more details about setting configuration features). For example, to provide the licenseFileLocation in PHP:

SaxonC-HE is an open-source product. The primary license is the Mozilla Public License version 2.0. In most cases, the source files are marked as being "incompatible with secondary licenses", which means that the code cannot be combined with code issued under a GPL license (the reason for this is the difficulty of contacting all past contributors to gain their assent).
Some components are licensed under the Apache version 2.0 license or under BSD-style licenses. For more information see the Licenses section on the main Saxonica website.

Although SaxonC technically adheres to the definition of open source software, there are practical limitations. Specifically, the "Source Code Form" of the product, in the terminology of the MPL license, consists primarily of Java source code, and in order to build SaxonC from the Java source code, you need access to the Excelsor JET development tools, which are no longer commercially available to new users.

section.title: PHP extension
section.p: The PHP extension is an interface module that allows SaxonC to be invoked from PHP applications.
Please have the following packages on your machine to build SaxonC for the PHP language: make, php-devel, (php8.X-dev, tested on 8.1.11), apache2 or httpd, gcc-c++ or g++ (minimum C++14).
SaxonC should already have been installed following the instructions at Installing SaxonC.

section.title: Python extension
section.p: The Python extension is an interface module that allows SaxonC to be invoked from Python applications. The SaxonC 12 Python extension requires Python >=3.8 (64-bit).

SaxonC is now officially available as a wheel package available on pypi. This means that it can be installed with pip, which greatly simplifies the installation process. If however you are not able to install with pip, then the manual install and build instructions are provided below.

The simplest way to install the Python extension is to use pip. This will install the right package for your platform (Linux, Mac OS, or Windows). You just need to specify which edition of the product you want (EE, PE, or HE).

On Windows, install Python 3.X (64-bit) with VS 2017 or 2019 which can then be run with command "py" from Powershell.

section.title: Troubleshooting
section.p: After installing SaxonC, if you notice anomalies in execution, then the apache log file usually has useful information on errors reported and crashes. See below for a description of some of the common errors and crashes, and their solutions:

p.code: PHP Warning: PHP Startup: Unable to load dynamic library '/usr/lib/php/modules/saxon.so' - libsaxonhec.so: cannot enable executable stack as shared object requires: Permission denied in Unknown on line 0

li.p: This has been observed on centos systems when SELinux is enforced/enabled.
Solution: Run the following command to show the security setting for the library files:
Then run the following commands or similar to change the security context:

p.code: Unable to load C:\Program Files\Saxonica\SaxonHEC1.2.1\libsaxonhec.dll Error: : No error

li.p: Caused by attempting to run SaxonC in 32-bit environments, including 32-bit Python and PHP builds. SaxonC can only run with 64-bit builds.
Solution: The machine operating system must be 64-bit, and Python and PHP builds must be 64-bit to run with SaxonC.
